reasoningChain.evidence: I want to keep progressing while learning the newly rescued character options.
Trying the newly rescued mage produced clear useful evidence: it ranked first in damage and the team won, so another visible no-cost character experiment is attractive.
The berserker is a newly visible complete melee damage hero, while the drummer ranked fourth with about 5% damage in the latest fight and is currently perceived as very weak.
I can replace the drummer with the berserker now without spending a visible resource.
This keeps the proven warrior and mage plus the healer, while changing the current member with the weakest recent damage contribution.
If the berserker's risky melee output is useful, it should rank among the top two damage contributors in the next combat.

hypothesis.problem: The drummer's direct combat contribution fell to the lowest rank in the last fight.
hypothesis.cause: The newly rescued berserker may add stronger damage than the drummer while the healer offsets some of its visible low-health risk.
